title: Tenant reservation watermarking and safety allocator
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently allocate reservation credits to tenants based on static commitments + a simple burst pool. This leads to two problems: (1) long-lived underutilized reservations that waste capacity during pressure windows, and (2) brittle low-latency guarantees when many tenants simultaneously consume burst tokens. This PR introduces a reservation watermarking and safety allocator that dynamically adjusts effective reservations, reclaims idle headroom, and enforces safety caps during overload.

High-level design: We add two concepts to the fleet allocator: a low watermark (committed floor) and a reclaim watermark (soft cap above committed). When tenant utilization falls below the reclaim watermark for a configurable idle window, the allocator tags the reservation as reclaimable and moves that capacity into an ephemeral pool. Conversely, during load surges the allocator will respect a safety cap per-tenant (configurable percentage of total fleet) to avoid noisy-neighbor collapse. The allocator integrates with the autoscaler and the burst pool — reclaimed capacity is visible to the burst pool and prioritized by fairness score.

Behavioral changes: - Reservations are no longer binary; they carry dynamic effective_reservation values computed from watermarks and recent utilization histograms. - Ephemeral pool uses LRU-style aging and per-tenant priority buckets (production, critical, standard) to decide assignment. - Safety caps prevent any single tenant from consuming more than X% of cluster capacity; X is a runtime knob that can be tuned per-fleet. - Preemption: when safety caps are hit, lower-priority ephemeral allocations are preempted before cutting into committed floors.

Files changed (high-level): allocation/allocator.go (new watermark logic), allocation/ephemeral_pool.go (LRU aging + priority queues), autoscaler/integrations.go (hook for reclaimed capacity), api/v1/reservation.proto (expose watermarks and effective_reservation), telemetry/metrics.yaml (new metrics), observability/dashboards/reservation-overview.json, e2e/tests/reservation_reclaim_test.go, pkg/config/fleet_defaults.yaml, docs/allocator.md (design doc + knobs), small client changes in sdk-go and sdk-python to surface new reservation fields.

Commits (summary): - introduce reservation watermark structs and histogram-based utilization tracker - implement reclaimable tagging and ephemeral pool assignment - safety cap enforcement and preemption path - autoscaler integration to treat reclaimed capacity as available headroom - add metrics/tracing and dashboard wiring - unit + e2e tests + docs + SDK surface fields

Testing and results: Unit tests cover watermark transitions and preemption paths. E2E benchmark on a 50-GPU staging fleet reproduces a 7-day mixed-tenant workload: compared to baseline, median request latency at 95th percentile improved 8-12% for standard tenants under bursty arrival patterns, and overall cluster utilization increased from 64% to 78% during daytime peaks. Tail regressions under a simulated hot-tenant were prevented by safety caps; we observed negligible SLA violations in the runs.

Rollout plan: Feature gate behind fleet.experimental.reservation_watermarks (off by default). Canary rollout to 2 fleets (dev and staging) for 48 hours with telemetry alerting on reclamation_rate and preempt_count. If stable, enable on low-risk production fleets for 72 hours, then full roll once autoscaler equilibrium metrics are stable.

Related: ENG-7684 implements the reclamation telemetry; ENG-7710 tracks dashboard and alerting changes. SUP-2102 was an incident prompting earlier manual reclamation of idle reservations.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing the committed billing model or customer-visible reservation guarantees; effective_reservation is an internal serving-time construct and is surfaced in telemetry and SDK only for observability.

review_conversation: Marcus Li (reviewer): Can you clarify the durability semantics when a reclaimed allocation is preempted? Would that trigger immediate cancellation of in-flight requests?

Author (Aisha): Good question. We only preempt ephemeral allocations, which are never guaranteed for in-flight requests. In-flight requests under ephemeral allocation are given a 300ms drain window communicated via the runtime; if they exceed that, the request will be rejected with a 429 and logged under preempt_count. Committed floors are never preempted.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): I ran the stress job and saw a spike in scheduler CPU with the histogram computations. Can we cache the bucket summaries and only recompute every 500ms?

Author (Aisha): Implemented a lightweight sliding-window summary cache and moved the histogram crunch to the allocator worker thread. CPU overhead dropped ~40% in my microbenchmarks; pushed a follow-up commit
Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): We need an ops kill-switch in case reclaiming causes instability in a fleet. Suggest a runtime flag to set reclaim_rate to 0 and a dashboard panel to flip it.
Author (Aisha): Added fleet.experimental.reclaim_rate (float, default 0.2) and an Ops runbook entry in docs/allocator.md. Also added an unsafe_disable_reclaim boolean for emergency toggles.

Marcus Li: Approval after the CPU cache change and runbook additions.

performance_summary: Staging 50-GPU run with replayed multi-tenant traffic: utilization baseline 64% -> 78% with watermarks; P95 latency for standard tenants improved 8-12% under burst windows; safety caps prevented a simulated hot-tenant from consuming >32% of fleet capacity in tests.
release_notes: Introduce reservation watermarking and ephemeral reclamation that increases fleet utilization and reduces tail latency under bursty traffic. Feature is gated and off by default; ops knobs allow immediate disable. See docs/allocator.md for runtime knobs and runbook.
testing_instructions: 1) Enable feature gate fleet.experimental.reservation_watermarks=true on a canary fleet. 2) Observe telemetry: reclamation_rate, preempt_count, effective_reservation histogram. 3) Run e2e/tests/reservation_reclaim_test.go. 4) If preempt_count rises above threshold, flip unsafe_disable_reclaim=true and investigate.
notes_for_release_manager: Keep feature gated by default. Coordinate with SRE to canary on two non-critical fleets for 72 hours. Attach perf artifacts from perf-bench job to the release ticket. Ensure billing/legal are aware that committed billing semantics haven't changed.
incident_reference: SUP-2102: manual reclamation performed during high-traffic incident (feb 2026) motivated this work
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: overly-aggressive reclamation could increase 429s for ephemeral workloads. Mitigation: conservative default reclaim_rate=0.2, safety caps, drain window, and emergency disable flag. Telemetry alerts added for rapid rollback.
docs: docs/allocator.md (design + ops), observability/dashboards/reservation-overview.json, sdk-go and sdk-python docstrings updated
